facts.text: Build, buy or partner is the decision between developing simulation capability in-house on open-source parts, buying commercial products, or paying an outside company to deliver the capability.
facts.quote: Build, buy or partner is the decision between writing the simulation capability in-house on open-source parts, buying commercial products, or paying an outside company to deliver it.

facts.text: Building simulation capability in-house on open source using CARLA, Isaac Sim or Gazebo, Chrono, and Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) offers the lowest license cost but requires the highest internal labor.
facts.quote: Build in-house on open source (CARLA or Isaac Sim or Gazebo, Chrono, Robot Operating System 2 or ROS 2): lowest license cost, highest internal labor

facts.text: Building simulation capability in-house on open source provides full ownership of source and models, but entails no vendor support, key-person dependence, and responsibility for all credibility evidence.
facts.quote: full ownership of source and models, but no vendor support, key-person dependence and the organization owns all the credibility evidence.

facts.text: Buying an integrated commercial simulation stack lowers the integration burden, but domain modeling and correlation work remain substantial.
facts.quote: Buy an integrated commercial stack: lower integration burden, but domain modeling and correlation remain substantial

facts.text: Buying an integrated commercial simulation stack does not provide ownership of the core and entails off-road gaps, license dependence, and roadmap risk.
facts.quote: the core cannot be owned, and there are off-road gaps, license dependence and roadmap risk.

facts.text: Buying specialist simulation tools and integrating them internally offers high flexibility but creates high interface and version complexity.
facts.quote: Buy specialist tools and integrate internally: high flexibility, high interface and version complexity.

facts.text: Partner-led implementation of simulation capability is potentially the fastest option, but knowledge and models stay with the partner and the dependency can become permanent.
facts.quote: Partner-led implementation: potentially fastest, but knowledge and models stay with the partner and the dependency can become permanent.

facts.text: The booklet judges a hybrid simulation implementation—an internal owner, a partner, and commercial or open-source tools—to offer the best balance of retained knowledge and outside specialization, provided the contract has unusually clear ownership clauses.
facts.quote: Hybrid: an internal owner plus a partner plus commercial or open-source tools, which the booklet judges the best balance of retained knowledge and outside specialization, provided the contract has unusually clear ownership clauses [Chapter 11].

facts.text: No independent benchmark from 2024 to 2026 states total cost, team headcount, or time to a first useful result for any of the five simulation implementation options.
facts.quote: no independent 2024 to 2026 benchmark states total cost, team headcount or time to a first useful result for any option

facts.text: Vendor case studies of simulation implementation options report large gains but are not controlled measurements.
facts.quote: vendor case studies report large gains but are not controlled measurements.

facts.text: Regardless of the simulation implementation option chosen, the booklet recommends that partner contracts require editable machine models, scene and source assets, parameter provenance, correlation datasets, test definitions, continuous-integration scripts, simulator version manifests, known-limitation registers, and interface specifications—not only test reports.
facts.quote: delivery of editable machine models, scene and source assets, parameter provenance, correlation datasets, test definitions, continuous-integration scripts, simulator version manifests, known-limitation registers and interface specifications, not only test reports [Chapter 11].

facts.text: With no internal simulation capability and nine months before hardware, the booklet calls hybrid implementation the most defensible choice.
facts.quote: With no internal capability and nine months before hardware, the booklet calls the hybrid the most defensible choice

facts.text: The booklet warns that outsourcing simulation capability alone solves the 2027 deadline while creating a larger long-term dependency.
facts.quote: outsourcing alone "solves the 2027 deadline while creating a larger long-term dependency" [Chapter 11].
